response: Yes, many emergency medical services (EMS) professionals believe they should participate in disease prevention. In fact, a growing number of EMS professionals think that their role should extend beyond emergency response to include preventive care and community health initiatives. This perspective recognizes the potential for EMS to play a key role in identifying health risks, providing education, and connecting patients with community resources to prevent illnesses and injuries. By participating in disease prevention, EMS professionals can help reduce the burden on emergency services, improve health outcomes, and enhance the overall well-being of the communities they serve.
